text: The constitutional executive operates through ministers and government under the Crown within legal and conventional limits.
limitation: This is a system-level synthesis, not a statement about a current officeholder or a justiciable rule in every circumstance.

text: Government and Parliament are distinct: government develops and implements policy while Parliament legislates, authorises taxation and spending, and scrutinises government.
limitation: A high-level institutional distinction; individual procedures have more specific rules.

text: A UK general election returns the House of Commons; the ability to command Commons confidence is central to forming and maintaining a government.
limitation: Constitutional conventions and exceptional circumstances cannot be reduced to a mechanical election result.

text: Ministers direct departments and are accountable to Parliament for government policy and administration.
limitation: Roles vary by department and statute; no current minister is identified.

text: The Home Civil Service supports the government of the day and is bound by statutory management provisions and the code values of integrity, honesty, objectivity and impartiality.
limitation: Northern Ireland has a separate Civil Service; the code does not turn administrative delivery into independent political authority.

text: The Scotland Act establishes the Scottish Parliament and Scottish Government framework and defines legislative competence through reservations and other limits.
limitation: Competence must be checked against the Act as amended for the exact provision; topic labels are insufficient.

text: The Government of Wales Act establishes the Senedd and Welsh Government framework and defines legislative competence through reservations and other limits.
limitation: Competence must be checked against the Act as amended for the exact provision; topic labels are insufficient.

text: The Northern Ireland Act establishes the Assembly and Executive framework and distinguishes transferred, reserved and excepted matters subject to statutory limits.
limitation: Institutional operation and competence must be checked for the date and exact matter.

text: Devolution is asymmetric: Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland have different statutory competence tests, institutions and routes.
limitation: This comparison does not decide competence for any proposal.

text: Local authorities are public bodies with functions set by legislation and territorial arrangements; directory placement alone does not prove a power.
limitation: This release does not enumerate councils, functions or local-government statutes across all four nations.

text: Bills pass through parliamentary stages and require Royal Assent before becoming Acts of Parliament.
limitation: Bill type and procedure vary, and an Act's provisions may commence at different times.

text: Where delegated legislation is made as a statutory instrument, it depends on power in an enabling Act and follows the route specified by that Act and the applicable statutory-instrument procedure.
limitation: Not all delegated legislation uses the same form; the enabling power, procedure, territorial extent, commencement and later amendments must be checked instrument by instrument.

text: Codes, manuals, standards and service guidance describe conduct or practice but are not silently treated as Acts or delegated legislation in this atlas.
limitation: A particular document may still have legal relevance; this classification is not legal advice.

text: The Constitutional Reform Act and judiciary guidance protect judicial independence; courts decide disputes, including citizen-versus-state disputes, under law.
limitation: The cited explanatory page is England-and-Wales focused; court structures and routes differ across UK legal jurisdictions.

text: Government needs Parliamentary approval for taxation and for the public spending authorised through Supply and related legislation.
limitation: Specific taxes, Estimates, funds and statutory authorities have distinct procedures.

text: HM Treasury leads economic and public-finance policy and operates spending-control and public-money frameworks.
limitation: A role description and guidance do not replace Parliamentary or statutory authority.

text: HMRC is a non-ministerial department that administers taxes, payments and customs functions within its statutory responsibilities.
limitation: This does not state a live tax rate, liability, filing result or HMRC endorsement.

text: Strategic tax policy and tax administration are distinct functions: Treasury leads policy while HMRC administers and advises on implementation within its role.
limitation: Exact statutory responsibilities and devolved taxes must be checked separately.

text: Supply Estimates set out departments' requests for resources and cash for Parliamentary approval; a plan, Estimate, appropriation and outturn are not interchangeable.
limitation: The process includes supplementary and other instruments not exhaustively mapped here.

text: The Consolidated Fund is a central account into which public revenues are paid and from which authorised issues are made under the public-finance framework.
limitation: Historic and later statutes interact; this is a map of the authority chain, not accounting advice.

text: The Comptroller and Auditor General's statutory comptroller function concerns the grant of credit for authorised issues from the Consolidated Fund and National Loans Fund.
limitation: The exact statutory mechanism and fund must be checked; audit and policy choice remain distinct.

text: The Office for Budget Responsibility provides independent fiscal and economic analysis under its statutory framework; its forecasts do not authorise tax or spending.
limitation: Forecast requirements and the fiscal framework can change.

text: The National Audit Office supports Parliament by auditing bodies and accounts within its remit and examining value for money, without setting the policy objectives examined.
limitation: Audit scope and statutory access vary by body and engagement.

text: The House of Commons Public Accounts Committee scrutinises value for money, economy, efficiency and effectiveness using evidence that includes National Audit Office work.
limitation: Committee membership, inquiries and recommendations change over time.

text: Government Banking Service provides banking and payment services to public-sector customers; that operational rail is separate from legal authority to tax or spend.
limitation: No bank account, payment instruction, provider contract or live transaction is exposed.

text: Government departments and public bodies develop and deliver policy and services; their directory listing does not by itself establish a particular legal power.
limitation: The live organisation directory changes and this release does not claim a complete body inventory.

text: The GOV.UK Service Standard supplies service-design expectations for government teams.
limitation: A standard is not legal authority, proof of compliance or a universal technology architecture.

text: GOV.UK One Login is a shared sign-in and identity-checking capability for participating government services.
limitation: Sign-in does not establish eligibility, liability or decision authority; this atlas performs no authentication.

text: GOV.UK Notify is a shared channel for participating public services to send messages.
limitation: This atlas sends no message and stores no contact detail.

text: GOV.UK Pay is a shared payment capability for participating public services.
limitation: Payment processing is not authority, entitlement or proof of liability; this atlas takes no payment.

text: GOV.UK Forms is a shared capability for government teams to create online forms.
limitation: This atlas embeds no form, submits no data and does not imply every service uses the product.

text: The GOV.UK API Catalogue helps locate public-sector APIs published into the catalogue.
limitation: Catalogue presence is not a guarantee of availability, fitness, authority or data quality; this build calls no API.

text: data.gov.uk is a discovery service for data published by central government, local authorities and public bodies.
limitation: Each dataset has its own publisher, rights, freshness, coverage and quality limits.

text: Identity, messaging, payment, forms, APIs and data discovery can carry service interactions but do not themselves confer legal competence or decision authority.
limitation: The legal basis, controller, eligibility rule and decision-maker must be established for each service.

text: HMRC provides a service-complaint route, which is distinct from challenging a tax decision through review or appeal.
limitation: The correct route and deadline depend on the issue; starting a complaint may not protect an appeal deadline.

text: Some HMRC decisions can be reviewed by HMRC or appealed to the tax tribunal under the applicable rules.
limitation: Rights, exclusions, payment rules and deadlines vary by decision; this is not tax or legal advice.

text: The First-tier Tribunal (Tax) hears eligible tax appeals independently of HMRC under its jurisdiction and procedure.
limitation: Eligibility, form, fee, time limit and onward appeal depend on the matter and current rules.

text: The Parliamentary and Health Service Ombudsman investigates eligible complaints about UK government departments and the NHS in England after required prior steps.
limitation: Jurisdiction, the Parliamentary route, prior steps and time limits must be checked.

text: The Freedom of Information Act creates rights to request recorded information from covered public authorities, subject to its scope and exemptions.
limitation: Other information regimes, exemptions and territorial rules may apply.

text: The Information Commissioner's Office provides a complaint route for eligible concerns about official information after applicable prior steps.
limitation: The information regime, internal review requirement and deadlines must be checked.

text: In England and Wales, judicial review is a court procedure for reviewing the lawfulness of public decisions or failures to act; it is not a general merits appeal.
limitation: This route is scoped to England and Wales. Procedure, permission, standing, alternative remedies and strict time limits require current legal advice.

text: The Scottish Public Services Ombudsman provides a route for eligible complaints about public services in Scotland.
limitation: Jurisdiction, prior complaint steps and time limits must be checked.

text: The Public Services Ombudsman for Wales provides a route for eligible complaints about public services in Wales.
limitation: Jurisdiction, prior complaint steps and time limits must be checked.

text: The Northern Ireland Public Services Ombudsman provides a route for eligible complaints about public services in Northern Ireland.
limitation: Jurisdiction, prior complaint steps and time limits must be checked.

text: Complaint, statutory review, tribunal appeal, ombudsman referral, information-rights complaint and judicial review are distinct routes, not one automatic ladder.
limitation: Choosing a route and protecting a deadline can require professional advice; this atlas makes no eligibility determination.

text: The Crown, House of Commons and House of Lords are constituent parts of Parliament; Royal Assent is the Crown's formal agreement to an approved Bill.
limitation: The constitutional role is mapped without current monarch details or any inference of personal discretion.

text: Parliamentary sovereignty is a constitutional principle under which the UK Parliament is the supreme legal authority and can create or end law.
limitation: The principle and its interaction with devolution, rights and constitutional law are complex; this atlas offers no legal conclusion for a dispute.

text: The UK Supreme Court is the final court of appeal for eligible civil cases across the UK and eligible criminal cases from England, Wales and Northern Ireland under its jurisdiction.
limitation: Jurisdiction, permission and originating legal system must be checked; Scottish criminal cases follow a different final route.

text: Local-government structures and functions are nation-specific: an England guide cannot be applied silently to Scotland, Wales or Northern Ireland.
limitation: This release maps four distinct entry points but does not enumerate every council, power, duty or reorganisation.

text: The English Devolution and Community Empowerment Act 2026 changes parts of England's devolution and local-government framework through provisions whose commencement and implementation must be checked.
limitation: A newly enacted provision is not assumed commenced or implemented merely because it appears in the Act.

text: The Bank of England has statutory and institutional monetary and financial-stability roles that remain distinct from Treasury fiscal policy, Parliamentary Supply and HMRC tax administration.
limitation: This atlas does not model monetary-policy decisions, rates, prudential rules or individual financial regulation.

text: The Bank of England operates RTGS for settlement in central-bank money and operates CHAPS; these payment-system rails are distinct from the public-spending authority chain.
limitation: This is a system boundary, not access to RTGS, CHAPS, a bank account or transaction execution.

text: The Payment Systems Regulator regulates designated payment systems within its remit; regulation, operation and settlement are distinct roles.
limitation: The atlas does not determine regulatory jurisdiction or resolve an individual payment complaint.

text: A legislation.gov.uk record can distinguish original and revised text and signal outstanding effects; a contents link alone does not prove that every provision is in force or fully updated.
limitation: The current status, amendments, commencement and territorial extent must be checked on the exact provision.

text: The Open Government Licence permits reuse of information expressly made available under it subject to conditions and exclusions, and does not permit implied official status or endorsement.
limitation: This atlas is link-only for official sources and does not assume every linked item or component is covered by OGL.

text: The UK Statistics Authority and Office for National Statistics operate within the statutory official-statistics system; published statistics retain methods, revisions and quality limits.
limitation: Official-statistics designation is not inferred for an arbitrary dataset, and no statistic is imported into this release.

text: A public-service data flow must establish its own legal roles, purpose and safeguards; a shared API or identity product does not supply that basis.
limitation: This public snapshot and runtime collect no personal data and make no determination of a controller, processor or lawful basis. Exact vendor captures have the separate scope documented in NOTICE.

text: The Local Government and Social Care Ombudsman provides a route for eligible complaints about councils and certain services in England within its remit.
limitation: Jurisdiction, provider coverage, prior complaint steps and time limits must be checked.
